title: Structural Insights into Phosphorylation-Mediated Polymerase Function Loss for DNA Polymerase beta Bound to Gapped DNA.
authors: Srivastava, Amit; Idriss, Haitham; Homouz, Dirar
one_liner_zh: 该文通过微秒级分子动力学模拟研究DNA聚合酶beta与缺口DNA复合物中磷酸化诱导的构象变化，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作机制研究，方法为物理模拟，但对象非TF-DNA体系，故评6分。
abstract: DNA polymerase beta is a member of the X-family of DNA polymerases, playing a critical role in the base excision repair (BER) pathway in mammalian cells by implementing the nucleotide gap-filling step. In vitro phosphorylation of DNA polymerase beta with PKC on S44 causes loss in the enzyme's DNA polymerase activity but not single-strand DNA binding. Although these studies have shown that single-stranded DNA binding is not affected by phosphorylation, the structural basis behind the mechanism underlying phosphorylation-induced activity loss remains poorly understood. Previous modeling studies suggested phosphorylation of S44 was sufficient to induce structural changes that impact the enzyme's polymerase function. However, the S44 phosphorylated-enzyme/DNA complex has not been modeled so far. To address this knowledge gap, we conducted atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of pol beta complexed with gapped DNA. Our simulations, which used explicit solvent and lasted for microseconds, revealed that phosphorylation at the S44 site, in the presence of Mg ions, induced significant conformational changes in the enzyme. Specifically, these changes led to the transformation of the enzyme from a closed to an open structure. Additionally, our simulations identified phosphorylation-induced allosteric coupling between the inter-domain region, suggesting the existence of a putative allosteric site. Taken together, our results provide a mechanistic understanding of the conformational transition observed due to phosphorylation in DNA polymerase beta interactions with gapped DNA. Our simulations shed light on the mechanisms of phosphorylation-induced activity loss in DNA polymerase beta and reveal potential targets for the development of novel therapeutics aimed at mitigating the effects of this post-translational modification.
abstract_zh: DNA聚合酶β是DNA聚合酶X家族的一员，通过在碱基切除修复（BER）通路中执行核苷酸缺口填补步骤，在哺乳动物细胞中发挥关键作用。DNA聚合酶β在体外经PKC磷酸化S44位点，导致酶DNA聚合酶活性丧失，但不影响单链DNA结合。尽管这些研究表明单链DNA结合不受磷酸化影响，但磷酸化诱导活性丧失机制背后的结构基础仍知之甚少。先前的建模研究表明，S44磷酸化足以诱导影响酶聚合酶功能的结构变化。然而，S44磷酸化酶/DNA复合物迄今尚未被建模。为解决这一知识空白，我们对pol beta与缺口DNA复合物进行了原子级分子动力学模拟。我们的模拟采用显式溶剂并持续微秒级时间尺度，揭示了在Mg离子存在下，S44位点的磷酸化诱导了酶显著的构象变化。具体而言，这些变化导致酶从闭合结构转变为开放结构。此外，我们的模拟识别出磷酸化诱导的域间区域变构偶联，提示存在一个推测的变构位点。综合来看，我们的结果提供了对DNA聚合酶β与缺口DNA相互作用中因磷酸化而观察到的构象转变的机制性理解。我们的模拟阐明了DNA聚合酶β中磷酸化诱导活性丧失的机制，并揭示了开发新型治疗策略以减轻这种翻译后修饰影响的潜在靶点。
